section: Centre-State financial relations - Articles 264-293; taxes assigned, grants-in-aid, borrowing powers
subsections: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them
Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status
Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Under which Article of the Constitution are statutory grants-in-aid to needy States, including grants for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas, provided?
accepted.x: Statutory grants-in-aid are provided under Article 275 on the recommendation of the Finance Commission. They include grants for needy States and for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific Article governing statutory grants from the nearby Article on discretionary grants.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding grants-in-aid:
1. Statutory grants under Article 275 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Discretionary grants under Article 282 may be made for any public purpose.
3. Statutory grants are made on the recommendation of NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: statutory grants under Article 275 are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission, not NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong recommending authority by separating the constitutional body from the advisory policy institution.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 275 — Grants recommended by the Finance Commission
Article 282 — Grants charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Article 280 — Discretionary grants for any public purpose
accepted.x: Article 275 provides for statutory grants recommended by the Finance Commission. Article 282 concerns discretionary grants for public purposes, while Articles 280 and 293 concern the Finance Commission and borrowing respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the Article–function pair and reject options that assign a neighbouring financial provision to the wrong Article.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s: With reference to discretionary grants under Article 282, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
They are intended exclusively for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas.
They can be made only on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.
They may be made for any public purpose and were historically administered through the Planning Commission.
accepted.x: Article 282 permits discretionary grants for any public purpose. Historically, the larger part of such Central grants was associated with the Planning Commission; they are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
accepted.tq: Discriminate discretionary grants by their broad purpose and non-charged character.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Central grants?
o: Statutory grants — recommendation of the Finance Commission
Discretionary grants — recommendation of the Finance Commission as a constitutional requirement
accepted.x: Discretionary grants under Article 282 are not subject to a constitutional requirement that they be recommended by the Finance Commission. Statutory grants under Article 275 are linked to the Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Locate the option that wrongly transfers the constitutional recommendation mechanism from statutory to discretionary grants.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s: Grants in lieu of export duty on jute have been associated with which group of States?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha
Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
accepted.x: The special grants in lieu of export duty on jute are associated with Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete geographical list rather than selecting a group based on general regional similarity.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory vs discretionary → Article

accepted.s: A shift in the composition of transfers from grants-in-aid to tax devolution generally results in:
o: A reduction in unconditional transfers to States
An increase in unconditional or untied transfers to States
An increase in the Central parameters attached to every transfer
accepted.x: Tax devolution is formula-based and generally untied. Therefore, shifting from grants to tax devolution increases the share of unconditional transfers available to States.
accepted.tq: Apply the distinction between untied tax devolution and conditional grants to identify the consequence of a compositional shift.
accepted.sec: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tax devolution is generally formula-based and untied.
2. Centrally Sponsored Scheme grants may contain Central parameters and matching-share requirements.
3. A rise in tax devolution necessarily eliminates all grants to States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because an increase in tax devolution does not eliminate all forms of grants to States.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the two precise distinctions between devolution and scheme grants.
accepted.sec: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the vertical share of the divisible pool recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended a 41 percent share of the divisible pool for the States. The 42 percent figure relates to the Fourteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced percentages associated with successive Finance Commissions.
accepted.sec: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them

accepted.s: The budget estimate of tax devolution for 2024–25 was:
accepted.x: The budget estimate of tax devolution for 2024–25 was ₹12.47 lakh crore. The figure of ₹12.87 lakh crore represents the indicated scale of tax devolution for that year, not the budget estimate.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the actual or indicated scale from the specifically stated budget estimate.
accepted.sec: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them

accepted.s: On which date was the report of the Sixteenth Finance Commission tabled?
accepted.x: The report of the Sixteenth Finance Commission was tabled on 1 February 2026. 12 February 2026 relates to the reported acceptance of its devolution recommendations by the Centre.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related dates connected with tabling and acceptance.
accepted.sec: Grants vs tax devolution - effect of a shift between them

accepted.s: The constitutional ceiling on profession tax under Article 276(2) is:
accepted.x: Article 276(2) permits profession tax up to ₹2,500 per person per year. The earlier ceiling was ₹250.
accepted.tq: Identify the present ceiling rather than the earlier figure retained as a distractor.
accepted.sec: Profession tax - Article 276 ceiling, amendment

accepted.s: The ceiling on profession tax was raised from ₹250 to ₹2,500 by the:
accepted.x: The Sixtieth Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 raised the profession-tax ceiling under Article 276 from ₹250 to ₹2,500 per annum.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment number and year with the specific monetary change.
accepted.sec: Profession tax - Article 276 ceiling, amendment

accepted.s: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969 for the distribution of Central Plan assistance during the:
accepted.x: The Gadgil formula, associated with D. R. Gadgil, was introduced in 1969 during the Fourth Five Year Plan for distributing Central Plan assistance among States.
accepted.tq: Link the formula to its year and Plan period rather than to the later Gadgil–Mukherjee formula.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s: Under the Gadgil formula, which criterion carried the highest weight?
accepted.x: Population carried the highest weight under the Gadgil formula, at 60 percent. Per-capita income, tax effort, ongoing irrigation and power projects, and special problems each carried 10 percent.
accepted.tq: Identify the dominant weight in the formula instead of selecting one of the equal secondary criteria.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Gadgil formula — distribution of Central Plan assistance among States
Gadgil formula — appointment of the Finance Commission
Gadgil formula — determination of profession-tax ceilings
Gadgil formula — settlement of inter-State legal disputes
accepted.x: The Gadgil formula was used for the devolution or distribution of Central Plan assistance among States. It was not related to constitutional taxation limits, Finance Commission appointments or judicial disputes.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy domain associated with the formula and reject unrelated constitutional functions.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s: Special category States traditionally received Central Plan assistance on which terms?
o: 100 percent grant without any loan component
accepted.x: Special category States received Central Plan assistance on the favourable basis of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan, with the grants treated as a first charge on such assistance.
accepted.tq: Recall the grant–loan ratio and reject the more familiar but incorrect rounded alternatives.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a parameter traditionally associated with special category status?
o: Strategic location along an international border
High per-capita income and commercially viable State finances
Low population density or a sizeable tribal population
accepted.x: Special category parameters included difficult terrain, low population density or sizeable tribal population, strategic border location, economic and infrastructural backwardness, and non-viable State finances. High per-capita income and commercially viable finances were not such parameters.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed economic condition among otherwise recognised special-category characteristics.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The Gadgil and Gadgil–Mukherjee formulas lost their earlier role in intergovernmental transfers.
Reason (R): The Planning Commission was abolished and Plan grants ended.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the abolition of the Planning Commission together with the ending of Plan grants explains why the formulas lost their earlier role.
accepted.tq: Test whether the institutional change stated in the Reason directly explains the policy consequence in the Assertion.
accepted.sec: Plan transfer formulas - Gadgil, Gadgil-Mukherjee; special category status

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Part XII of the Constitution is correct?
o: It deals with Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits and includes Articles 264 to 300A.
It deals exclusively with the powers of local governments.
It extends from Articles 352 to 360 and regulates financial emergencies alone.
It contains only provisions relating to elections and emergency powers.
accepted.x: The specified financial-relations framework is located in Part XII, which begins at Article 264 and includes provisions on finance, property, contracts and suits. The notes specifically identify Articles 264–293 as the financial-relations range relevant here.
accepted.tq: Use the Part-and-Article range to distinguish financial provisions from other constitutional Parts.

accepted.s: Article 265 of the Constitution embodies which principle?
o: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
No State may borrow without approval of the President.
No grant may be made without approval of Parliament.
No expenditure shall be incurred without approval of the Finance Commission.
accepted.x: Article 265 provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact constitutional wording associated with the authority-of-law requirement for taxation.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Which pair of Articles is correctly associated with the Consolidated Funds, Public Accounts and Contingency Fund?
accepted.x: Articles 266 and 267 deal respectively with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts, and the Contingency Fund.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article pair and distinguish fund provisions from revenue-distribution and borrowing provisions.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
2. Article 281 relates to the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
3. Articles 292 and 293 deal with borrowing by the Union and the States respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Articles 280 and 281 concern the Finance Commission and its recommendations, while Articles 292 and 293 concern Union and State borrowing respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each Article against its constitutional subject before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a tax generally included among the State-exclusive taxes?
accepted.x: Customs duty on imports is not a State-exclusive tax. State-exclusive taxes include agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol, taxes on land and buildings, and land revenue, among others.
accepted.tq: Identify the Union-domain tax among a list of State taxation subjects.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only taxes or levies associated with the State domain?
o: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles
Customs duty, corporation tax, Union excise duty and income tax
Goods and Services Tax, customs duty, wealth tax and corporation tax
Surcharge on Union taxes, customs duty, export duty and corporation tax
accepted.x: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles are included among taxes associated with the State domain. The other sets consist predominantly of Union taxes.
accepted.tq: Separate the State tax field from familiar Union taxes by checking every item in the set.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Under Article 285, which of the following is the general constitutional position?
o: State property is exempt from all Union taxation without exception.
Union property is taxable by States whenever it is used for commercial purposes.
Union property is exempt from State taxation.
Neither Union nor State property can ever be taxed.
accepted.x: Article 285 generally exempts Union property from State taxation. The corresponding provision in Article 289 concerns exemption of State property from Union taxation, subject to the rule relating to commercial activity.
accepted.tq: Compare Articles 285 and 289 without reversing the Union–State direction of the exemption.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Articles 285 and 289?
o: Article 285 concerns exemption of Union property from State tax, while Article 289 concerns exemption of State property from Union tax, subject to taxation of commercial activity.
Article 285 concerns State borrowing and Article 289 concerns Union borrowing.
Both Articles exclusively exempt State property from Union taxation.
Both Articles deal only with the distribution of divisible taxes.
accepted.x: Article 285 addresses the exemption of Union property from State taxation. Article 289 addresses the exemption of State property from Union taxation, with commercial activity being taxable as specified.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of taxation—Union property versus State property—to avoid a reversed comparison.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: A dispute between the Union and a State concerning a legal right may be instituted in the Supreme Court under its original jurisdiction. The relevant Article is:
accepted.x: Article 131 confers original jurisdiction on the Supreme Court in disputes involving legal rights between the Union and one or more States or between States.
accepted.tq: Match the intergovernmental dispute mechanism with the Article conferring original jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding fiscal matters and Article 131 is correct?
o: Every matter referred to the Finance Commission must be decided by the Supreme Court under Article 131.
Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from the scope of Article 131.
Article 131 applies only to disputes between private persons and States.
Article 131 abolishes the advisory role of the Finance Commission.
accepted.x: Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from the scope of Article 131. Article 131 concerns original suits involving qualifying legal-right disputes between the Union and States or among States.
accepted.tq: Reject the overbroad statement by distinguishing a constitutional reference to the Finance Commission from an original suit.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes

accepted.s: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are generally:
o: Judicial orders enforceable without further governmental action
Legally binding in every respect on the Union Government
Binding only on State Governments and never considered by the Union
Advisory and not binding, though they are ordinarily not rejected without compelling reasons
accepted.x: Finance Commission recommendations are not legally binding. However, the Rajamannar view emphasises that they should not ordinarily be rejected without compelling reasons.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutional recommendation from binding adjudication and note the convention of reasoned acceptance.
accepted.sec: Part XII (Articles 264-293) - content, state-exclusive taxes, fiscal disputes
